title: Long-Term Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy in Participants with Primary Biliary Cholangitis of Saroglitazar Magnesium-V on Clinical Outcomes (EPICS-V)
official: A Phase 3b/4, Multicenter, Parallel-Group, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Two-Arm, Long-Term Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Saroglitazar Magnesium on Clinical Outcomes in Participants with Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effect of QD dose of saroglitazar magnesium (1 mg, oral) compared to placebo, based on time to the first occurrence of the defined clinical outcome events in participants with PBC.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Each participant must meet all of the following criteria to be enrolled in this study: 1. Is capable of understanding the written informed consent, provides signed and  witnessed written informed consent, and agrees to comply with protocol requirements.
2. 2. Is an adult male or female, must be ≥18 years of age at the time of signing informed  consent.
3. 3. Is receiving UDCA at the standard recommended dose of 12 to 16 mg/kg/day for ≥12 months with a stable dose within this range for ≥6 months prior to  screening, and expected to remain on a stable dose during the study period. OR Is unable to tolerate UDCA and did not receive UDCA in the past 3 months prior to  screening.
4. 4. Has a history of confirmed PBC diagnosis, as demonstrated by the presence of ≥2 of  the following 3 diagnostic factors: i. A history of elevated ALP levels for ≥6 months prior to screening. ii. Positive antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) titer based on the validated assay-specific cut-off for positivity OR if AMA is negative, then  positive PBC-specific antibodies (anti-GP210 and/or anti-SP100 and/or  antibodies against the major M2 components [PDC-E2, 2-oxo-glutaric acid  dehydrogenase complex]). iii. Liver biopsy consistent with PBC diagnosis.
5. 5. Has documented evidence of cirrhosis (as defined below) and has ALP >ULN and TB ≤5 × ULN. Evidence of cirrhosis at baseline will be based on one of the following criteria: i. Prior liver biopsy showing the presence of cirrhosis (Ludwig or Scheuer  Stage 4 [Ludwig et al 1978] or Fibrosis score 3 in the fibrosis component of  the Nakanuma scoring system [Nakanuma et al 2010]). OR ii. Has liver stiffness measurement (LSM) value >15 kPa, as assessed by screening FibroScan AND associated with any one of the following: o Radiologic evidence of cirrhosis (nodular liver and splenomegaly, as  defined by local radiographic standards). o Platelet count <140 × 10⁹/L.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Participants meeting any of the following criteria will be excluded from the study: 1. Has consumption of 2 standard alcohol drinks per day (or 14 alcohol drinks per week)  if male and 1 standard alcohol drink per day (or 7 alcohol drinks per week) if female  for ≥3 consecutive months (12 consecutive weeks) within 5 years prior to screening.  (Note: 1 standard alcohol drink = 12 ounces [~360 mL] of beer, 4 ounces [~120 mL] of wine, or 1 ounce [~30 mL] of spirits/hard liquor.)
2. 2. Has known CPT B (having a score of ≥7) or CPT C (having a score of ≥10) cirrhosis  classification at screening.
3. 3. Has a Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD)-Na score of ≥12 at screening.
4. 4. Has a history or presence of any of the following other concomitant liver diseases at  screening: i. Chronic hepatitis B or hepatitis C virus (HBV or HCV) infection.  a. Participants with positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) will be  excluded. Participants who have seroconverted (HBsAg-negative and  hepatitis B surface antibody [HBsAb)–positive) may be included in this  study.  Note: If a participant tests negative for HBsAg, but positive for HBcore  antibody, the participant would be considered eligible if the absence of  HBV DNA is confirmed by HBV DNA polymerase chain reaction reflex  testing performed in the central laboratory. b. Participants with chronic HCV infection (ie, positive HCV antibody  and evidence of HCV RNA) will be excluded. Note: If a participant has been treated for the HCV infection and has been  cured for a duration of >2 years prior to screening, they may be enrolled in  the study. ii. Primary sclerosing cholangitis. iii. Alcohol-associated liver diseases. iv. Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH)-PBC overlap syndrome. Note: The Paris criteria are commonly used to define the presence of PBC with  features of AIH and have been endorsed by the EASL and the AASLD.  The investigator should ensure that these criteria are assessed during the eligibility  evaluation and exclude any participant who meets them (Section 15.2). v. Hemochromatosis.  vi. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis on historical biopsy.  vii. α-1 antitrypsin deficiency.. Note: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency will be assessed based on the participant’s medical history and available medical records. Where alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency cannot be adequately excluded, appropriate testing will be performed locally and the result reviewed by the Investigator prior to randomization.
5. 5. Has a history or presence of clinically significant hepatic decompensation, including  the following: i. Liver transplantation or currently registered on a liver transplant list. ii. Ascites requiring treatment. iii. History of variceal bleeding or related interventions (eg, variceal banding, or  transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt [TIPS] placement). iv. Hepatic encephalopathy Grade ≥2 per West Haven criteria (Vilstrup et al  2014); a history or presence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.  v. Hepatorenal syndrome (Type I or II). vi. Known or suspected hepatocellular carcinoma or other hepatobiliary  malignancies, as determined by α-fetoprotein [AFP] >20 ng/mL. For remaining exclusion criteria please refer to the Protocol.
